title: Cold rebuild: A reading report
summary: Rebuild A reading report from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A reading report** in *Loading related data*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: seed.Authors.Add(new Author { Name = "Le Guin", Books = [new() { Title = "Earthsea" }, new() { Title = "The Dispossessed" }] });
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db");
steps.explain: Without `Include`, `Books` is just the empty list the class starts with: nothing was loaded. With it, both of Le Guin's books arrive in the same query.

steps.title: Rebuild A reading report cold
prompt: The tests give you the model below. Write `List<string> Report(LibraryDb db)` that returns, for every author **ordered by name**, a line like

listing the author's books ordered by title, each with its number of reviews. An author without books prints `Name:` with nothing after the colon. Load the data with **one** query using `Include` and `ThenInclude`.
class Author { public int Id; public string Name; public List<Book> Books; }
class Book   { public int Id; public string Title; public int AuthorId; public Author Author; public List<Review> Reviews; }
class Review { public int Id; public int Stars; public int BookId; public Book Book; }
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
